expectations.text: Report identifies Get()'s comment/behavior contradiction (claims empty string, actually throws std::out_of_range) and ranks it at/near the top
expectations.evidence: Item 2 in the High severity section: "claim `Get()` 'returns ... an empty string' ... `sessions_.at(session_id)` ... throws `std::out_of_range` ... the code explicitly throws `std::out_of_range`"; second finding overall, near the top.

expectations.text: Report flags the nonexistent 'timeout_s' parameter in Get()'s comment
expectations.evidence: Item 1: "`Get()` header comment documents a parameter that does not exist ... The function has no `timeout_s` parameter ... a stale comment left over from an earlier signature."

expectations.text: Report flags the header comment duplicated into the .cc as a wrong-place/drift problem
expectations.evidence: Item 9: "Duplicated declaration comment on `Get()`'s definition (`session_store.cc:7-8`) ... Duplicating doc comments invites drift — which has already happened here ... The contract belongs in the header only."

expectations.text: Report flags the undocumented ttl_s_ negative-value sentinel (never expires)
expectations.evidence: Item 6: "The implementation checks `ttl_s_ >= 0` before expiring ... meaning a negative TTL makes sessions immortal. The constructor comment ... says nothing about this."

expectations.text: Report flags Get()'s undocumented side effect of evicting the expired entry on read
expectations.evidence: Item 3: "Calling `Get()` on an expired session silently evicts it from the store (mutating state) and throws. Neither the eviction side effect nor the throwing contract is mentioned anywhere."

expectations.text: Report flags the Author: line for removal
expectations.evidence: Item 13: "`// Author: bob@example.com` — author attributions in file headers are discouraged ... because they go stale; version control tracks authorship."

expectations.text: Report flags Delete()'s imperative mood / missing period
expectations.evidence: Item 11: "'Delete the session and return whether it existed' uses the imperative mood and lacks a terminating period."

expectations.text: Report flags the commented-out code in Put() and recommends deletion
expectations.evidence: Item 4: "The 'old implementation kept for reference' block is dead code preserved in comments. Version control is the place for history" — flags it and recommends it not remain (removal via version control history).

expectations.text: Report flags the malformed TODO above Purge()
expectations.evidence: Item 5: "`// TODO fix this later` violates common TODO conventions ... it names no owner, no bug/issue reference, and ... gives no hint of what is broken in `Purge()`."

expectations.text: Report flags '/* notify */ false' as not conforming to /*param_name=*/value form
expectations.evidence: Item 7: "`Evict(session_id, /* notify */ false);` uses the wrong spacing/format ... The conventional (clang-tidy/Google) form is `/*notify=*/false`."

expectations.text: Findings ordered by severity: wrong/contradictory comments before missing contracts before formatting noise
expectations.evidence: The Medium tier puts noise/formatting items before missing-contract items: commented-out code (item 4) and malformed TODO (item 5) rank above the undocumented ttl_s sentinel (item 6), and the /*notify=*/ format issue (item 7) ranks above undocumented Evict() (item 8) — missing contracts do not precede formatting noise.

expectations.text: Report gives file/line references and does not modify the sources
expectations.evidence: Every item cites file:line (e.g. `session_store.h:15-18`, `session_store.cc:32`); report states 'No code was changed' and both source files still contain all planted defects.

summary.notes: Finds all planted defects with good line references and unmodified sources, but its severity ordering interleaves formatting noise (dead code, TODO, argument-comment format) above missing-contract findings, violating the required wrong > missing > noise ordering.
